The lounge host flagged a thought on bedding supplies after a rushed handover and the note was passed straight to the Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways. Bedding supply issue and passenger discomfort

The cabin team had already been told to keep a close eye on a pet lounge setup, but the handover from the earlier shift was thin and the bedding stock on the cart did not match the room count. A traveler noticed the shortage while preparing for boarding and said the resting area looked bare. Diego Mendes was seen checking the pen area, and Luna stayed calm but began to pace when the surface was adjusted too many times. The senior coordinator moved in fast, replaced the bedding with clean spare items, and asked the lounge host to keep watch for any further changes in comfort.

A short side note came from the same thread about cabin heat, because the traveler wanted a clear path if the animal area became too warm. speaker: <<FACT F117>> The record was kept open while the crew confirmed the temperature stayed steady and the pet was not left without care. No further distress was seen after the bedding swap, but the team still treated the handover gap as a service fault that could have become a bigger problem in flight.

The handling steps were simple and immediate. The stray stock count was corrected, the lounge setup was checked again, and the crew was reminded to verify bedding before any transfer. One traveler also reported mild skin irritation from handling the rough surface, so the conversation was taken seriously and the document trail was updated at once. speaker: <<FACT F113>> The lounge host then agreed to log supply checks more carefully and to flag any missing comfort items before boarding starts.

Follow-up will be to review the handover note, refresh the supply list, and remind the cabin team to report any animal-care concern without delay. The matter is still being watched and the desk expects cleaner handling next shift. Companion Animal Travel Desk
